speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to my office. I see you are a newborn presenting with a generalized rash; to help me understand what you're experiencing, can you please describe when the rash first appeared and if it seems to spread or change? Additionally, have you noticed any fever, poor feeding, or lethargy? 

REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, Blood_Culture

speaker: Patient
text: 4-day-old newborn. The newborn was born at term with no complications. The mother had no prenatal care and has a history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. The newborn presents with a generalized rash that has been present for 1 day.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized erythematous maculopapular rash and pustules. I also have Rash with an erythematous base, Rash over the trunk and extremities, Sparing of the palms and soles. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand your concern; please stay calm while I review the lab results for your blood count and cultures. Given the description of erythematous maculopapular lesions with pustules on an erythematous base and sparing of the palms and soles, could you confirm if your baby is a premature infant born around 28–32 weeks gestation?

REQUEST IMAGES: Full body skin photograph showing the rash distribution and pustule morphology.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Born at term, no prenatal care for the mother, mother's history of gonorrhea treated 4 years ago. Social history: N/A for the newborn.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Gonococcal Infection. The presence of pustules with an erythematous base sparing the palms and soles in a newborn born to a mother with a history of gonorrhea is classic for disseminated gonococcal infection. REQUEST TEST: Gram stain of pustular fluid; REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up dermoscopy of the pustules.
